title: workspace-sync commit 4a5b8115 (2026-07-07) silently reverted 5 git-owned files that decider had just modified — root-cause the smart_copy path that allowed it, add pre-push gate for multi-writer git-owned files, and audit whether other silent losses landed in the same window. Investigation of ISS-2953 escalation.

context.why_now: Decider's 2026-07-09T02:08Z run's forensic audit surfaced ISS-2953: workspace-sync commit 4a5b8115 silently reverted expansion-tracker.json backward, dropping the freshly-allocated EXP-654 and orphaning ISS-2941. The reversion was DISCOVERED only because this run's decider allocated a NEW EXP-654 for unrelated work (ISS-2952 cross-WIN terminology) and the pre-push Section-7 integrity gate caught the resulting duplicate-id-across-live/archive violation. Without that gate the loss would have been permanent and invisible. Operator inspection of commit 4a5b8115's file list shows the reversion was NOT limited to expansion-tracker.json — workspace-sync touched 5 git-owned files with clear reversion patterns.

explicit_violations_of_CLAUDE_md_ownersh: data/wins.json is git-owned per OWNERSHIP table — workspace-sync MUST NEVER push FUSE→git for this file. It did.
docs/index.html is git-owned per OWNERSHIP table (generated by build.js) — workspace-sync MUST NEVER push FUSE→git for this file. It did.
monitor/decisions/open-issues.json is git-owned (decider is the sole writer) — workspace-sync MUST NEVER push FUSE→git for this file. It did.

monitor/analyst/expansion-tracker.json is in the 'Unclassified — Known multi-writer files' list per CLAUDE.md (analyst + analyst-baby + decider). Not listed in workspace-sync.md NEVER_PUSH. But the CLAUDE.md discipline states 'Do not add to OWNERSHIP in build.js or NEVER_PUSH in workspace-sync.md' — meaning workspace-sync is EXPECTED to handle it correctly via the smart_copy universal-pusher logic. The mechanism failed here.

context.recovery_state: This morning's decider run (2026-07-09T02-08) recovered by renaming its new allocation to EXP-655 and restoring the original EXP-654 + ISS-2941 records verbatim from commit 82399139. It ALSO fixed 3 other issues found in the forensic audit (ISS-2954/2955/2956 all self-verified and closed). But that recovery relied on decider's Section-7 pre-push gate catching the duplicate — a fortuitous circumstance, not a durable safety net. If the same reversion recurs and doesn't produce a duplicate-id collision (which is the ONLY signal decider currently has), the loss would be silent and permanent.
context.prior_related_class: This LOOKS like a variant of FND-02 (2026-05-30T09:11Z queue-history.jsonl destructive overwrite, commit 3c62327) that PROP-065 was supposed to close. FND-02 established that workspace-sync's mtime + anti-reversion is INSUFFICIENT for clone-and-push .jsonl files — FUSE content byte-matched a historic commit yet anti-reversion didn't fire. PROP-065's fix was git-append-only classification for 26 .jsonl files. But the FND-02 root cause — smart_copy incorrectly deciding to push a stale FUSE version — was NOT fixed for non-.jsonl git-owned files, because PROP-065's scope was strictly .jsonl. If the same mtime-guard-insufficient class recurs on data/wins.json + docs/index.html + open-issues.json, we have a much bigger problem than PROP-065 addressed.

questions_to_answer: Q1 — Fetch commit 4a5b8115 in full (parent, tree, diff) and identify EXACTLY which workspace-sync code path (smart_copy universal-pusher, Step 4c divergence handler, or something else) generated the reversion.

Q2 — What was the state of FUSE for each of the 5 files at 04:05Z? Was FUSE older than the decider's 02:23Z commit for each file? If yes, why did workspace-sync's mtime + anti-reversion guard not fire? If FUSE was NEWER, what content did it hold?

Q3 — Which specific line in workspace-sync.md's smart_copy pseudocode was executed for each of the 5 files? Trace the classification decision: were data/wins.json/docs/index.html/open-issues.json checked against the git-owned OWNERSHIP list? If yes, why did smart_copy still push? If no, why not?

Q4 — Is this the FND-02 mtime-guard-insufficient class applied to non-.jsonl files, or a different mechanism entirely (e.g., a workspace-sync run that clone-and-pushed WITHOUT a git-pull first, so its local main HEAD was stale)?

Q5 — Are there other commits in the last 30 days from workspace-sync with the same reversion signature (touching data/**, docs/**, or monitor/decisions/open-issues.json)? Search git log for workspace-sync commits that modified any of those paths and cross-check against decider commits in the preceding 4 hours.
part_A_forensic_root_cause.investigation_scope: Read workspace-sync.md, sync-workspace-step4c.js, monitor/scripts/*.js for anything smart_copy related. Fetch the actual git commit contents. Do NOT modify code in this part — just investigate and report.
part_A_forensic_root_cause.output: Report at monitor/tinker/reports/workspace-sync-reversion-4a5b8115-forensics-2026-07-09.md answering Q1-Q5 with commit citations and code line refs.

part_B_preventive_pre_push_gate.why: Even if Part A finds the specific root cause, defense-in-depth: workspace-sync should have a pre-push gate that BLOCKS a push if it would revert any of the 5+ multi-writer or nominally-git-owned files backward.
part_B_preventive_pre_push_gate.shape: Model on PROP-121 (workspace-sync lint-workspace-sync-push.js hook, which already catches bulk-delete threshold). Add a new check to that hook: for a defined SENTINEL_FILES list (initially: expansion-tracker.json, attention-inbox.json, open-issues.json, wins.json, docs/index.html), compute the git HEAD content hash vs what workspace-sync is about to push. If the push would BYTE-REVERT any sentinel file to a prior git commit's content (walk git log to check), abort the push with a clear error message identifying the target file + the earlier commit whose content matches the push.
part_B_preventive_pre_push_gate.constraint: This must be BYPASS-PROOF via git-hook enforcement (PROP-121 pattern). Do NOT put the check in the prompt where the LLM agent can silently skip it. Do NOT use --no-verify.
part_B_preventive_pre_push_gate.output: PROP-127 (or whatever next PROP id) authored with the design + code diff for the pre-push hook extension. Verification pattern grade B: replay of commit 4a5b8115 in a fixture must be BLOCKED by the extended hook.

part_C_retroactive_audit.why: The Q5 sweep in Part A may find other silent reversions. If it does, we need to reconstruct what was lost and where possible replay decider's work.
part_C_retroactive_audit.shape: For each additional reversion found in Q5: (a) identify what content was lost, (b) check whether subsequent decider runs recovered it (as this morning's did for EXP-654), (c) if not, file a follow-up HNOTE with the recovery plan.
part_C_retroactive_audit.output: Table in the Part A report listing all identified reversions from the 30-day sweep with recovery status per case.

constraints.no_experimental_config_changes: Do NOT modify workspace-sync.md, sync-workspace-step4c.js, or any config in this directive without first landing the forensic report. Investigate → report → propose (via PROP) → then ship.
constraints.prop_051_disaster_class_review_required: The pre-push hook in Part B changes workspace-sync's push behavior. Any change to workspace-sync's push behavior is PROP-051-class — one bad hook implementation could BLOCK workspace-sync entirely, which would degrade FUSE→git rescue latency. Design the hook so a bug in the check FAILS OPEN (allows the push) or FAILS TO A CLEAR EXIT rather than silently blocking. Include this discipline in the PROP.
constraints.do_not_disable_workspace_sync: Do NOT pause dome-workspace-sync scheduled task while investigating. Steady-state FUSE→git rescue is more valuable than perfect safety during the investigation window; and the 2026-07-07 reversion appears to be a one-off pattern (not observed daily), so the risk of running-while-fixing is low.
